cards.title: Letters that stand for numbers
cards.body: A variable is a letter that stands for a number you don't know yet — usually x. An expression like 3x + 5 is a recipe: multiply x by 3, then add 5. The moment you learn x, you can compute the whole thing.

cards.title: The parts have names
cards.body: In 4x + 7, the 4 is the coefficient (it multiplies the variable), x is the variable, and 7 is the constant (it never changes). Knowing the names makes every later step easier to talk about.
Like terms are twins: 3x and 5x can combine into 8x because the x matches. But 3x and 3x² are NOT like terms — different exponents, no combining. Match the letter AND the power.
Simplify 2x + 7 + 5x − 3: group the x's (2x + 5x = 7x) and the constants (7 − 3 = 4). Answer: 7x + 4. Two groups, two additions, done.

cards.explain: Like terms need the same variable with the same exponent. Only 4x and 9x qualify.

flashcards.back: A letter (usually x) that stands for an unknown number.
Terms with the same variable raised to the same power, e.g. 3x and 5x.

questions.q: What does the expression 5n − 2 mean in words?
choices: Multiply 5 by n minus 2, all times 5
questions.explain: Read left to right following order of operations: 5n means 5 times n, then take away 2.

questions.q: Why can't 4x² + 3x combine into one term?
questions.explain: Like terms need matching variables AND exponents. x² and x are different powers.

questions.q: A taxi charges $3 plus $2 per mile. Which expression gives the cost for m miles?
questions.explain: The per-mile rate (2) multiplies the miles, then add the flat fee: 2m + 3.

cards.title: Undo to solve
cards.body: An equation like x + 7 = 12 is a balanced scale. To find x, undo what's been done to it — using inverse operations. Addition undoes subtraction, multiplication undoes division. Whatever you do to one side, do to the other.

cards.title: One step, then two
cards.body: x + 5 = 11 → subtract 5 from both sides → x = 6. That's one step. For 2x + 3 = 11, undo in reverse order: subtract 3 first (2x = 8), then divide by 2 (x = 4). Peel the onion from the outside in.
Always check your answer by plugging it back in. If x = 4, then 2(4) + 3 = 11. It balances — you're right. Thirty seconds of checking saves full marks.
Solve 3x − 8 = 10: add 8 to both sides → 3x = 18. Divide by 3 → x = 6. Check: 3(6) − 8 = 18 − 8 = 10. Balanced.

cards.explain: Undo the −9 with its inverse: add 9 to both sides, giving x = 13.

flashcards.back: An operation that undoes another: addition/subtraction, multiplication/division.

flashcards.front: Why do both sides get the same operation?
flashcards.back: An equation is a balanced scale — change one side only and it stops being equal.

questions.explain: Add 2 → x/3 = 7, then multiply by 3 → x = 21.

questions.q: Maya's answer is x = 5 for 3x + 1 = 16. How does she verify it?
choices: Solve it a different way only
questions.explain: Substitution is the gold standard: 3(5) + 1 = 16 balances, so x = 5 is correct.

cards.title: The coordinate plane
cards.body: Two number lines cross to make a grid: x runs left-right, y runs up-down. A point like (3, 2) means go 3 right, 2 up. The spot where they cross, (0, 0), is called the origin.

cards.title: Slope: how steep?
cards.body: Slope measures a line's steepness: rise over run. Go up 2 for every 3 right and the slope is 2/3. Positive slope climbs left-to-right; negative slope falls; zero slope is flat; undefined slope is vertical.
y = mx + b is the cheat code: m is the slope, b is where the line crosses the y-axis. In y = 2x + 1, the line climbs 2 per step and crosses at (0, 1). Read a line without plotting a single point.
Graph y = −x + 4: it crosses the y-axis at 4 (b = 4) and falls 1 for every 1 right (m = −1). Plot (0, 4), then step down-right to (1, 3), (2, 2) — connect the dots.

cards.q: In y = 3x − 2, what is the y-intercept?
cards.explain: The y-intercept is b, the constant term: −2. The line crosses the y-axis at (0, −2).

flashcards.back: Go 3 units right on x, then 2 units up on y.
Rise over run — how steep a line is.

flashcards.front: In y = mx + b, what are m and b?
flashcards.back: m is the slope; b is the y-intercept.

flashcards.front: What does a zero slope look like?

questions.q: A line passes through (0, 5) and rises 2 for every 1 right. What's its equation?
questions.explain: Slope m = 2, y-intercept b = 5, so y = 2x + 5.

questions.q: What is the slope of the line through (1, 2) and (4, 8)?
Which line is steeper: y = 4x + 1 or y = 2x + 9?
questions.explain: Steepness comes from |m|. |4| > |2|, so the first line climbs faster.

questions.q: The equation y = −3 describes which line?
questions.explain: No x term means slope 0 — every point has y = −3, a flat horizontal line.

questions.q: Two lines have the same slope but different intercepts. How do they relate?
questions.explain: Same slope means same steepness; different intercepts mean they're offset — parallel lines.
